ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows an abrupt PN junction. The left side is labeled P+ region, with NA >> ND. The right side is labeled N-region, with ND = 10^16 /cm^3. The depletion width on the N side is marked as Xn between the junction and the depletion edge in the N region. Reasoning: Since the image indicates NA >> ND, this is a one-sided P+N junction, so most of the depletion region lies on the N side. For an abrupt junction, the peak electric field magnitude at the metallurgical junction is Emax = q ND Xn / epsilon_si. Given Xn = 0.2 micrometer = 2e-5 cm, ND = 10^16 cm^-3, q = 1.6e-19 C, and epsilon_si = 1.044e-12 F/cm. Substituting: Emax = (1.6e-19)(1e16)(2e-5)/(1.044e-12) V/cm = 3.07e4 V/cm. Converting to kV/cm gives Emax = 30.7 kV/cm.
